target_customer: Cities, contractors and fleet operators that run street sweepers or other low speed vehicles
problem: Street sweeping needs drivers and purpose built vehicles. Hermes sells autonomy retrofit kits that let existing vehicles run at low speed without a driver.
business_model: Retrofit kit sales and autonomy as a service; pricing from third-party directories is unverified
product_category: Low speed vehicle autonomy retrofit, street sweeping

founders.name: Guilhem Herail
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as sole founder with no background; Crunchbase profile lists him as Founder, CEO and CTO.

competitors.name: Trombia Technologies (Trombia Free)
competitors.what: Purpose built autonomous electric street sweeper from Finland
competitors.traction_then: Launched October 2020 with pilots planned for 2021 and deliveries in 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Retrofitting arbitrary vehicles with safe autonomy needs drive by wire control, perception and safety validation, even at low speed, for a one person team.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of exclusive customers or data; sweeper makers and retrofit software firms could build equivalents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sweeper makers have shown or sold autonomous sweepers (Trombia 2020; Boschung 2024); no source shows Hermes being bought.

market_need_then: Municipalities faced driver and labor costs and there was press interest in autonomous street sweepers around 2020, but no sourced evidence of spend on retrofits.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain product copy: any vehicle, anywhere, at low speed

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; the name matches the luxury and logistics brand Hermes and other companies.

pivots.from: Autonomous street sweeping as a service
pivots.to: Autonomy retrofit kit for any low speed vehicle
pivots.why: Not stated; the company site now sells a kit while the YC page says sweeping as a service

outcome_analysis: Hermes Robotics is listed as active with a team of five, and its site now sells an autonomy retrofit kit rather than a sweeping service. No verified funding round, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is unclear, and aggregator totals of 125 thousand to 240 thousand dollars are unverified.
notes: Only aggregators report funding: CB Insights 240K over 3 rounds (latest seed 130K on 2021-02-01), Craft 125K, Standout 175K labeled Series A. None verified, so no round recorded. Founding year conflicts (2018 CB Insights, 2020 other profile). Some profiles wrongly describe a trucking or warehouse company. Pivot is inferred from the difference between the YC page and the company site and is undated. Completeness pass: The seed round (about 130K, 2021-02-01) rests on a single database (CB Insights); totals from other aggregators conflict (125K Craft and Extruct, 175K Standout) and are not summed.
